{{Short description|None}}

The following is a '''list of the highest-grossing films in the United States and Canada''', a market known as the '''North American box office''' or, in the United States [[film industry]], the '''domestic box office'''.<ref name="filmvictoria">{{#invoke:cite|web|url=http://www.film.vic.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0006/969/AA6_Genre_and_Intenational_BO.pdf |title=Genre and International Box office |publisher=[[Film Victoria]] / Government of [[Australia]] |access-date=June 16, 2012 |page=10 |quote='''North American box office''' statistics includes figures from both the United States and Canada as industry standard. |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120616134810/http://www.film.vic.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0006/969/AA6_Genre_and_Intenational_BO.pdf |archive-date=June 16, 2012 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="reuters">{{#invoke:cite|web|url=http://www.canada.com/entertainment/movie-guide/Think+Like+tops+North+American+office/6537819/story.html |publisher=[[Reuters]] via Canada.com |title=Think Like a Man tops '''North American box office''' |first=Lisa |last=Richwine |date=April 30, 2012 |access-date=June 16, 2012 |quote=...easily beat four new films to win the U.S. and Canadian box office race.... ''Think Like a Man'' led '''domestic''' charts with... |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120616134329/http://www.canada.com/entertainment/movie-guide/Think+Like+tops+North+American+office/6537819/story.html |archive-date=June 16, 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Nominal figures==
This is a list of the highest-grossing films in the U.S. and Canada in [[United States dollar|US dollar]]s, ranked by lifetime gross.<ref name=":0">{{#invoke:cite|web|url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/chart/top_lifetime_gross/|title=Top Lifetime Grosses|website=Box Office Mojo|access-date=December 6, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120519095339/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/alltime/domestic.htm|archive-date=2012-05-19|url-status=live}}</ref> This ranking does not adjust for [[inflation]]. 

The list also includes the initial gross without adjustments.

==Adjusted for ticket-price inflation==
This is a list of films ranked by ticket sales with adjustments for changes in ticket prices and/or inflation.

For films released in 2019 or earlier: [[Box Office Mojo]] tracks average ticket prices at theaters from 1910 to 2020.<ref name="Boxofficemojoadjusted">{{Cite web |title=How are grosses adjusted for ticket price inflation? |url=https://help.imdb.com/article/imdbpro/industry-research/box-office-mojo-by-imdbpro-faq/GCWTV4MQKGWRAUAP#inflation |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250207210012/https://help.imdb.com/article/imdbpro/industry-research/box-office-mojo-by-imdbpro-faq/GCWTV4MQKGWRAUAP#inflation |archive-date=February 7, 2025 |access-date=March 1, 2025 |website=Box Office Mojo}}</ref> The list here starts with their "Adj. Lifetime Gross" based on 2020 ticket prices,<ref name="Boxofficemojotickets">{{Cite web |title=Top Lifetime Adjusted Grosses |url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/chart/top_lifetime_gross_adjusted/?adjust_gross_to=2020 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241225172223/https://www.boxofficemojo.com/chart/top_lifetime_gross_adjusted/?adjust_gross_to=2020 |archive-date=December 25, 2024 |access-date=March 1, 2025 |website=Box Office Mojo}}</ref> and then applies [[Template:Inflation]] to further adjust to the equivalent in {{Inflation/year|US}}.{{Inflation/fn|US}}

For films released in 2020 or later: This list starts with the film's lifetime gross,<ref name=":0" /> and then applies [[Template:Inflation]] as if the entire lifetime gross was earned in the year of release, to further adjust to the equivalent in {{Inflation/year|US}}.{{Inflation/fn|US}}

Many of the films on this list were released prior to the availability of home video and have had multiple releases.

| 26
| ''[[Avatar (2009 film)|Avatar]]''
| align="center"| 2009
|align="right"|{{sort|77000000|{{#tag:ref|[[Box Office Mojo]]'s inflation adjusted list estimates ''Avatar'' sold 97,309,600 tickets by dividing the gross revenue by the cost of an average ticket, which was $7.50 in 2009. However, in the case of ''Avatar'', ticket sales were a combination of the three formats of standard projection, [[3D film|3D]] and [[IMAX]] used during its theatrical run. Since box office admissions are not tracked, the total number of admissions cannot therefore be accurately determined simply by dividing the gross receipts by the average ticket price. ''Box Office Mojo'' revised its estimate by taking into account the ticket prices for all three different formats, and determined that ''Avatar'' sold 75 million tickets by April 21, 2010, with an average price of almost $10 a ticket, by which time it had grossed $745 million of its $760 million total.<ref name="Ray Subers (2010-04-21)">{{#invoke:cite|web| first = Ray | last = Subers | title = 'Avatar' Strikes DVD | website=Box Office Mojo | url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/news/?id=2728&p=.htm|date=April 21, 2010 | access-date=April 21, 2010 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110606183734/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/news/?id=2728&p=.htm | archive-date = June 6, 2011 | url-status=live}}</ref> An extra $15 million of sales would be equivalent to about 2 million more ticket sales, at the average 2D ticket price of $7.50 in 2009; using this revision, ''Avatar'' probably sold closer to 77,000,000 tickets.<ref name=mojo>{{#invoke:cite|web| title = Adjusting for Ticket Price Inflation | url = https://www.boxofficemojo.com/about/adjuster.htm | website = Box Office Mojo | access-date=June 5, 2012 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110623171245/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/about/adjuster.htm | archive-date = June 23, 2011 | url-status=live}}</ref>}}}} 79,333,713
|align="right"| ${{formatnum:{{#expr:{{Inflation|US|721490000|2020}}+{{Inflation|US|24714024|2022}}}}}}<br />

===Factors in determining "adjusted gross"===
No one yet has calculated a truly precise and definite referential adjusted gross for a film, since doing so would have to take into account most (or all) of the following:
* Box office gross on ''initial'' release
* Ticket price at time of release, or its relative price to other commodities in a given year,<ref name=mojo /> in relation to general [[inflation]] and [[gross domestic product]].<ref name=Loma>{{#invoke:cite|web|url=http://www.usi.edu/business/mbea/2004/MBEA2004Final/movies.doc |title=2004 Proceedings of the Midwest Business Economics Association March 17 – March 19, Chicago, Illinois: How the Motion Picture Industry Miscalculates Box Office Receipts |first=S. Eric |last=Anderson |first2=Stewart |last2=Albertson |first3=David |last3=Shavlik |publisher=[[Loma Linda University]] |access-date=June 16, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120226011733/http://www.usi.edu/business/mbea/2004/MBEA2004Final/movies.doc |archive-date=February 26, 2012 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref>
* Economic conditions that may help or hurt the entertainment industry as a whole (theaters in 2008 lowered ticket prices to attract more viewers though the average ticket cost $7.00)<ref name=mojo />
* [[Population (human biology)|Population]] at time of release—to be used to calculate:
* Availability of films (number of theaters and screens, number of prints)
* Competition of other media ([[television]], [[internet]], [[home video]], [[film piracy]])<ref name=mojo />
* Total number of films in the marketplace at a given time<ref name=mojo />
* [[Screen quotas]] (no influence on [[United States|U.S.]] box office)
* Price differences: matinee and evening tickets,<ref name=boreport>{{#invoke:cite|web| url = http://www.boxofficereport.com/atbon/adjustedextra.shtml | title= $200 Million Adjusted Extra | first =Daniel | last = Garris | publisher=BoxOfficeReport.com | date = September 7, 2007 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20090304203910/http://www.boxofficereport.com/atbon/adjustedextra.shtml | archive-date=March 4, 2009}}</ref> roadshow tickets,<ref name=boreport/> or difference between rural and urban cinemas<ref name=Loma/>
* Length of release (number of weeks)<ref name=boreport/>

Further explanation of issues with calculating an adjusted gross can be found in the article for [[List of highest-grossing films#Highest-grossing films adjusted for inflation|List of highest-grossing films]].
